deadline.value: Apply by December 1, 2026 for Fall 2027 entry; fall entry only.
deadline.quote: The Neuroscience PhD program accepts applications for the Fall semester only | The deadline for applications is Dec. 1

gre_general.value: GRE scores are not considered for the Neuroscience PhD.
gre_general.quote: Biochemistry and Biophysics, Molecular and Cell Biology, Neuroscience: GRE scores are not considered in the admissions process.

also.quote: The GRE is no longer accepted as a part of your application.

gre_subject.value: The Psychology subject test is not considered for the Neuroscience PhD.
gre_subject.quote: Biochemistry and Biophysics, Molecular and Cell Biology, Neuroscience: GRE scores are not considered in the admissions process.

english_waiver.value: The Neuroscience FAQ exempts only citizens or graduates of listed countries, which do not include India, so Indian applicants need a test score.
english_waiver.quote: Students who are citizens of the following countries, or who have graduated from an accredited degree program within these countries, are exempt from this requirement

also.quote: Australia, Canada (except Quebec), Ireland, New Zealand, South Africa, USA and the United Kingdom.

supervisor.value: Applicants need not contact a faculty member before admission; every student rotates through four labs first.
supervisor.quote: It is not necessary for applicants to contact faculty members in advance of admission regarding joining their lab

also.quote: All Neuro PhD students must complete four research rotations in their first year

funding.value: All Neuroscience PhD students are guaranteed funding, including a fellowship, full tuition and health insurance.
funding.quote: Students are guaranteed funding, including a competitive fellowship, a full-tuition scholarship, and health insurance benefits.

entry_route.value: Applicants need a bachelor's degree to apply.
entry_route.quote: You must hold (or be about to earn) a bachelor’s degree from an accredited U.S. or international institution.

notes: The Neuroscience FAQ's English exemption list conflicts with the graduate school English-medium route; the department rule is recorded as the program value.
